title: A conserved transfer — design-system demonstration
goal: See how a transfer changes balances while conserving the total, staged with the design system.
coverage: Self-contained fictional demonstration; replace for production.

scenes.headline: Money moves
scenes.narration: Money moves. It doesn't vanish. To see why, we will find the total, follow the quantity, and check the balance.

scenes.headline: One fixed total
scenes.narration: Two accounts share one fixed total of 150 units. Hold on to that number.

scenes.headline: Follow the quantity
scenes.narration: Account A holds 100 units, and Account B holds 50. Now ten units leave Account A. While they travel, they are still counted: ten in transit. Then they arrive in Account B, and the total never changed. It is still 150.

scenes.headline: Changed and conserved
scenes.narration: Compare before and after. The balances changed: A fell to 90, and B rose to 60. The total did not. Check the total before you trust the movement.

scenes.headline: Four transfers later
scenes.narration: Repeat that four times. Four transfers later, the balances have swung up and down, but the total line stays flat at 150.

scenes.headline: Three steps
scenes.narration: Here is the method. Read any transfer in three steps. First, find the total. Next, follow the moving quantity. Last, check the balance.

scenes.headline: Check yourself
scenes.narration: Check yourself. If 25 units move from B to A, what is the total? Pause and think. Still 150. Moving units changes balances, not the total.
